summary: Fresh produce company SE Fruits and Vegetable Ltd. is planning an initial public offering in Pakistan next month to boost its export capacity, adding to a record year of listings in the country.

title: Absa CEO: Africa Expansion Plan Progressing Well
summary: Absa Group is exploring the possibility of converting its representative office in Nigeria into a merchant bank. Chief Executive Officer Kenny Fihla also said he sees opportunities in Uganda, Zambia, Tanzania, Angola. He spoke to Bloomberg’s Chief Africa correspondent, Jennifer Zabasajja, to discuss their plans after the group reported net income for the first half-year of 12.58 billion rand vs. 11.23 billion rand y/y. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Stockland Rises Most Since 1987 as Tax Rules Favor New Builds
summary: Shares of two of Australia’s largest property developers surged, with Stockland seeing its largest advance in about 40 years, as tax changes favoring new builds offered a potential boost to residential development.

title: UK Inflation Accelerates as Energy Bills Surge
summary: UK consumer prices climbed to a four-month high after energy bills rose, ending a short period of respite for hard-pressed British households. Matt Bunny of Bloomberg Economics has the details. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Adnoc Cuts to Murban Volumes Send Flagship Oil Grade Higher
summary: Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. plans to trim the amount of crude sold to Asian customers in August and September, according to people familiar with the matter — cuts that are already helping to push up the price of the flagship Murban oil grade.

title: Australia Rejects Far-Right Call to Slash Cigarette Taxes by 75%
summary: Australia’s government rejected the far right One Nation party’s call to slash cigarette taxes in order to reduce prices and cut crime, arguing instead for an intensified struggle against illegal tobacco flooding the country.

title: Optimism on Europe Returns to Pre-Iran War Highs: Taking Stock
summary: Investors increasingly favor European stocks over US peers as the region’s robust economic outlook proves more attractive at a time of surging AI spending.

title: India Stocks Top Indonesia as Asia’s Least-Favored in BofA Poll
summary: India has replaced Indonesia as Asia’s least-preferred stock market in a survey of fund managers by Bank of America Corp., signaling growing caution toward a market that’s among the world’s worst performers this year.

title: Bond Traders Look to Hedge Risk of Fed Rate Cuts in 2027
summary: Bond traders are looking to hedge the risk that the Federal Reserve pivots to cutting rates in 2027. The dovish wagers are at odds with recent moves in the Treasuries market, which saw yields on long-dated bonds climb to multiyear highs as a Fed on hold would keep inflation running above its target for longer. Bloomberg's Ven Ram has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: South Korea Exploring New Financial Hub Beyond Overcrowded Seoul
summary: South Korea is looking to create a new financial center outside the capital Seoul, as the government moves to ease over-concentration in the greater metropolitan area, which is home to more than half the country’s population.

title: Ethiopia’s Currency Sinks as Central Bank Burns Through Dollars
summary: Ethiopia is burning through billions of dollars in a frantic — and so far unsuccessful — bid to stem the selloff in its currency.

title: China Bonds Buck Global Selloff on Policy Divide With Peers
summary: Chinese long-end bond yields are tumbling as traders bet on further economic weakness, highlighting a growing divide with global markets where yields have soared to multi-year highs.
